title: Stitch + Surge Pro‑Forma: Latency vs. Unit Cost Scenarios
body:
Purpose:
This is a working pro‑forma comparing stitching (KV/decoder reuse across short sessions) against surge-oriented capacity (burst slots + prewarmed tiling) for mixed chat workloads. Focus: p50/p95/p99 latency impact vs. marginal token cost ($/1k tokens) under three realistic surge shapes. Goal is directional guidance for product knobs (default stitch window, surge reserve fraction) and a short set of customer‑facing talking points.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Stitching (aggressive prefix reuse) reduces marginal cost by 18–26% under sustained conversational sessions with low interturn gaps, with median latency unchanged and p99 improving slightly.
- During short microbursts (many single-turn queries), aggressive stitching gives minimal cost win and can slightly increase p95/p99 due to slotization contention if reserved surge capacity is too low.
- Hybrid policy (stitch enabled + 15% surge reserve) is the best default for PLG customers: ~12–18% cost reduction vs baseline and p99 within target for interactive UX.

Experiment design (synth workload):
- Model: redwood-x-large-v2 (fp16) and a quantized int8 variant (qint8) used for comparative rows.
- Two session classes: 
  1) Multi-turn sessions: 60% of traffic, average 7 turns/session, interturn gap mean 12s (exp dist).
  2) Single-shot queries: 40% of traffic, median 1 turn, high concurrency.
- Surge shapes: 
  A) Sustained ramp (40% sustained uplift for 15m)
  B) Microburst (600 qps spike for 30s, baseline 80 qps)
  C) Wave (3x short bursts spaced by 90s)
- Runtime knobs compared: stitch-window {0s, 30s, 90s}, reserved-surge {0%, 15%, 30%}, model variant {fp16, qint8}.
- Outputs: p50/p95/p99 for generation latency (ms), tokens/sec throughput, and incremental $/1k tokens estimate (includes GPU amortized + energy + prewarm overhead).

ASCII scenario summary table (selected rows):
---------------------------------------------------------------
Scenario            | p50  | p95  | p99  | $/1k tokens | notes
---------------------------------------------------------------
Baseline (no stitch) | 72ms | 310ms| 720ms| $0.45       | fp16, no reserve
Stitch30 + 0%res     | 74ms | 295ms| 700ms| $0.37       | stitch-window 30s (qv: -18% cost)
Stitch90 + 15%res    | 78ms | 260ms| 490ms| $0.39       | best p99/cost balance in waves
NoStitch + 30%res    | 68ms | 240ms| 520ms| $0.55       | lower latency, higher $
qint8 + Stitch90      | 85ms | 320ms| 680ms| $0.33       | cost-leader, slight median hit
Microburst (peak)    | 90ms | 760ms| 1450ms| varies     | without reserve p99 explodes
---------------------------------------------------------------
Notes on numbers: these are synthesised from our microbench tracewalk harness (batching=adaptive, kv-hitrate applied where stitch active). $/1k tokens folds in estimated prewarm overhead for surge reserves and amortized GPU-minute cost.

Visual (tiny ASCII econ-sparkline by scenario):
- Baseline cost:  ▁▂▃▅▇▇▇▇▇ (steady medium-high)
- Stitch30 cost:   ▁▁▂▃▅▆▆▆▇ (lower tail)
- qint8 stitch:    ▁▁▁▂▃▅▆▇▇ (lowest median)
- Reserve30 latency: ▁▂▃▃▂▁ (low jitter)
(These are qualitative summaries from per-quantile curves.)

Interpretation and trade-offs: 
- Stitching mechanics: prefix/KV reuse saves compute on decoder layers for repeated context windows. Savings scale with turn length and KV hit rate; in mixed workloads the effective hit-rate observed was 32–48% when stitch-window=90s.
- Latency interplay: stitching can increase coalescing of requests (good for throughput) but also can create contention for GPU slots when many sessions overlap; reserving a small surge pool (15%) absorbs microbursts and keeps p99 reasonable.
- Quantization: qint8 reduces $/1k tokens materially (~15–25%) but increases median latency due to slower kernel paths in our current runtime. This is a near-term software optimization target.

Recommended defaults (product knobs):
- Default stitch-window = 30s for hosted API (balances cost and per-turn freshness).
- Default surge-reserve = 15% for PLG tier, enable customer override for Dedicated.
- Expose "aggressive-cost-mode" toggle that combines stitch-window=90s + prefer-quantized (for advanced users).

Customer-facing bullets (for docs/FAQ):
- "We automatically reuse model state when you have quick follow-ups — this reduces per-token cost for multi-turn flows while keeping median latency similar."
- "For interactive workloads that see sudden spikes, we keep a small warm reserve so your p99 latency stays in touch-and-type range."
- "Quantized serving reduces your per-token bill; if you want the absolute lowest latency we recommend the Dedicated + reserved capacity option."

Open questions / next experiments:
1) End-to-end A/B with real traffic on a small customer cohort to validate KV hit-rate (current numbers from synthetic tracewalk).
2) Profiling qint8 kernel hotpaths to recover median latency (~aim: within 5–8% of fp16).
3) Evaluate cost of progressive stitching (decay window by turn count instead of time).
4) Explore prewarmed narrow-profile (smaller GPU slices) for microburst absorption to lower $/1k tokens of reserve.

Appendix: raw sample slice (multi-turn heavy wave scenario, stitch90 + 15%res, fp16)
- p50: 78ms
- p75: 136ms
- p90: 215ms
- p95: 260ms
- p99: 490ms
- avg tokens/sec per GPU slot: 860
- estimated $/1k tokens: $0.39 (GPU amort $0.32 + energy+infra $0.07)
